get.summary: Classify a pasted GitHub link without contacting GitHub
get.description: Pure validation. Only github.com is accepted, so this cannot be used to make the server request another host.

Reads the repository from the GitHub REST API when asked, through a short server-side cache, so values can be up to a minute old; `fetched_at` and `cache_status` say how old. Values are as GitHub reports them and nothing is stored. Private repositories are reported as not found. Answers 503 when the server has GitHub access switched off.

get.summary: Top contributors and latest release of a public GitHub repository
get.description: A separate, opt-in read: the ten accounts GitHub lists with the most contributions and GitHub's 'latest release'. It costs two more GitHub requests (three when the repository copy is older than a minute), which is why it is not part of the basic analysis. `contributors_status` is `listed`, `none` (GitHub has nothing to list) or `declined` (GitHub refuses to list them for very large histories); `latest_release` is null when the repository has no published release. Values are as GitHub reports them and nothing is stored. Private repositories are reported as not found. Answers 503 when the server has GitHub access switched off.

get.summary: A year of weekly commit counts for a public GitHub repository
get.description: A separate, opt-in read: commits on the default branch for each of the last 52 weeks, as GitHub reports them. GitHub computes these in the background, so the first ask can only be answered `status: computing` (GitHub's own 202); ask again a few seconds later. VYRON never waits for it. `none` means GitHub has no commit activity to report. Every ask, `computing` included, costs GitHub requests from the server's quota: one more than the repository read, which is itself reused for a minute. Only a ready answer is kept (for a minute); `computing` is never cached, in the server or in a browser, which is why this route sends no Cache-Control max-age. Values are as GitHub reports them and nothing is stored. Private repositories are reported as not found. Answers 503 when the server has GitHub access switched off.

get.summary: A package's declared dependencies, read from PyPI or npm
get.description: Reads one package from its registry's public JSON API when asked, through a short server-side cache (ten minutes), so values can be that old; `fetched_at` and `cache_status` say how old. It makes at most one registry request and follows no dependency: reading a dependency's own dependencies is another call. `dependencies` are the runtime requirements the package declares with no condition (PyPI) or the `dependencies` of the version tagged `latest` (npm); `left_out` counts what it declares but this read does not list (PyPI requirements under an extra or an environment marker; npm development, peer and optional dependencies). `requirement` is the version range as written, and `readable` is false when it points outside the registry (a URL, a path, an alias). A `sourced` label means the package's own metadata says it, nothing more: it does not say a package is maintained, popular or safe. Nothing is stored. Answers 503 when the server has registry access switched off.

get.summary: A package's release dates, read from PyPI or npm
get.description: Every version of one package with the date its registry records for it, oldest first, from the same registry document as the dependencies route (so one registry request can serve both, and the server keeps the answer for ten minutes: `fetched_at` and `cache_status` say how old it is). What a date means differs by registry and is stated in `date_meaning`: PyPI's is the earliest upload time among a version's files, npm's is the registry's own `time` entry. `pre_release` is read from the version number only. `left_out` counts versions the registry names that have no usable date, were unpublished (npm), carry an implausible date or an unusable version string; at most the newest 2000 releases are listed and `omitted_older` counts the rest. PyPI documents the `releases` key this reads as deprecated, so if a PyPI answer has no release dates the route answers 502 with that fixed reason. `sourced` means the registry records it, nothing more: it does not say how a package is maintained. Nothing is stored. Answers 503 when the server has registry access switched off.

get.summary: The server's current GitHub API quota
get.description: The quota the server's GitHub credentials have, as of the last response from GitHub (or a live read, which GitHub does not count). Answers 503 when GitHub access is switched off.

source_urls.description: The GitHub API URLs the values were read from: the evidence for the label.

contributions.description: Commits GitHub attributes to the account, as it reports them.

profile_url.description: Built by VYRON from a login that passes GitHub's naming rules. Null for bots.

LatestRelease.description: GitHub's 'latest release': the most recent release that is not a draft or pre-release, ordered by its created date (the date of the commit the release uses). That is GitHub's definition, not necessarily the highest version number.

source_urls.description: Every GitHub API URL the values rest on, including one whose answer was a 403 or 404.

days.description: Commits on each day, Sunday first.

total.description: GitHub's total for the week; it equals the sum of `days`.

CommitWeek.description: One week of commits on the default branch, starting on a Sunday at 00:00 UTC.

source_urls.description: Every GitHub API URL the values rest on, including one whose answer was a 202 or 204.

name.description: What to ask the registry for.

requirement.description: The version range as the package declares it. Null when none is given or when it is not plain version syntax.

readable.description: False when the requirement points outside the registry (a URL, a path, an alias), so the name does not identify a package there.

PackageLeftOut.description: Declared by the package but not listed in `dependencies`. `conditional` is a PyPI requirement under an extra or an environment marker; `unusable` is a name no registry could have issued.

license.description: As the maintainer wrote it; not validated.

registry_url.description: The package's page for people, built by VYRON from the checked name. Null when the values came from a stand-in rather than the registry.

source_url.description: The registry API address the values were read from: the evidence for the label.

pre_release.description: True when the version NUMBER looks like a pre-release (a PEP 440 a/b/rc/dev segment for PyPI, a `-` suffix for npm). A reading of the string, not something the registry says.

ReleaseEntry.description: One version and the date its registry records for it. `yanked` is PyPI's flag (every file of the version is yanked); `deprecated` is npm's.

ReleaseLeftOut.description: Versions the registry names that are not in `releases`. `undated`: no usable date came with the version. `removed`: npm still holds a date for a version that is no longer published. `implausible_date`: before 1991 or after the moment of the read. `unusable`: a version string no registry would issue.

registry_url.description: The package's page for people. Null when the values came from a stand-in.

omitted_older.description: Earlier releases left out to keep the list to 2000 entries.

source_url.description: The registry API address the values were read from: the evidence for the label.

PackageReleases.description: `date_meaning` says what a date is: `first_file_upload` (PyPI: the earliest upload time among a version's files) or `publish_time` (npm: the registry's own `time` entry).

ValidationError.description: A parameter or body field is invalid.

Forbidden.description: The session is not allowed to do this.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests; see the Retry-After header.

XRequestID.description: Echoes a valid inbound X-Request-ID, or a generated one.
